probe: Improve probe_frid to support both ARM and X86 To unify probing logic, we want to provide a new 'fdt_get_frid' as equivalent call to `acpi_get_frid`. The `probe_frid` then can support both X86 and ARM platforms. BUG=chromium:982692 TEST=emerge-$BOARD mosys Change-Id: I1d9b86441a1c470946db1c27a72b4e66a305ce7b Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1697964 Tested-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hsin-Yi Wang <hsinyi@chromium.org>

cros_config: Change cros_config_read_*sku_info* input array format The cros_config_read_* have different arguments: - ARM (fdt) versions need a list of identifiers and one length arg. - X86 versions take a single comma separated list Meanwhile, probe_frid and other functions take a string array with NULL in last element. To unify, we should always use NULL-terminated array and strlfind to look up list. BUG=chromium:982692 TEST=emerge-{kukui,octopus,eve} mosys; run 'mosys platform model' on device. Change-Id: I4bb38062d9b9ce57750d3224656b5c9f88e0c878 Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1697967 Tested-by: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Hung-Te Lin <hungte@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Hsin-Yi Wang <hsinyi@chromium.org>

cros_config: Generalize cros_config_read_sku_info for both x86 and ARM Currently the cros_config_read_*sku_info have different implementations per x86 and ARM. However, the logic is almost the same, if we can always probe with product names. This is a first step to unify both architecture. The new cros_config_read_sku_info is now supporting both x86 and ARM, by matching firmware name (which is a more precise match than SMBIOS product name). Note cros_config_struct.c is not changed yet, so the 2nd stage matching is still done by FDT compatible string. cros_config: Allow matching devices using firmware names Since multiple build target is introduced, matching based on FDT compatible string may easily go wrong (because the compatible string includes all base or reference names), especially if the SKU ID is the same for different models. In order to keep the FDT-compatible-string implementations untouched for legacy devices, cros_config_read_sku_info_struct is extended so we can specify different "match device" functions - either using probe_fdt_compatible or the new firmware ID approach. kerberos: Add Kerberos configuration validator The Kerberos daemon should not accept all options in a Kerberos configuration, but only a whitelisted subset. Thus, this CL adds a class to validate configuration data. See https://web.mit.edu/kerberos/krb5-1.12/doc/admin/conf_files/krb5_conf.html for a description of the format and a list of all options. It was necessary to implement a parser for the configuration since that functionality is not publicly exposed by the MIT krb5 library. The parser is loosely based on prof_parse.c:parse_line(), see https://github.com/krb5/krb5/blob/master/src/util/profile/prof_parse.c#L277, but with a less C-like implementation and only checked array access for security. BUG=chromium:978806 TEST=Unit tests Change-Id: I33f75b4f4441dfb5a1fbb81b0b01f72a0a59c71e Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1687882 Tested-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Commit-Ready: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Lutz Justen <ljusten@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Alexander Hendrich <hendrich@chromium.org>

kerberos: Validate Kerberos configuration Hooks up the ConfigValidator class added in a previous CL to actually validate the configuration sent via SetConfig. Validation makes sure that the syntax is correct and that only whitelisted config options are used. If a user in Chrome adds a new Kerberos account, the account does not exist yet when the user modifies the config. In order to still allow Chrome to validate config, a new D-Bus method, ValidateConfig, is added that does not require an account. Since config is an untrusted user input, parsing is done in a jailed separate process. Moreover, the config is run through the actual krb5 parsing code to make sure it accepts it as well. shill: metrics: Rename WiFiStatusType to WiFiReasonType The WiFiStatusType enum is used exclusively for representing the type of wifi disconnect reason. Since the standard uses "reason" to mean a disconnect reason and "status" to mean an auth/assoc status code, it makes sense to be consistent and use "reason" in this case. This change also fixes a bug in which kStatusCodeMax was used instead of kReasonCodeMax for the maximum value of a disconnect reason code (which likely occurred in the first place because the code did not consistently use "reason" when appropriate). cros-kernel2.eclass: Add support for generating compile_commands.json Recent kernels allow to generate a 'compilation database' with the compiler flags for each compilation unit. Other programs like LLVM tools or IDEs may use this information for analyzing C source code. Since Chrome OS kernels are built inside the chroot the default compilation DB 'compile_commands_chroot.json' contains chroot paths, which are meaningless for tools running outside the chroot. Also generate a version of the compilation DB with external paths ('compile_commands_no_chroot.json'). The *.json files are installed in /build/${BOARD}/build/kernel. To generate the compilation database the kernel must be built with 'USE=compilation_database'. The feature is only available for kernels that are built with clang (kernels >= 4.4 for most devices). BUG=none TEST= - USE=compilation_database emerge-cheza chromeos-kernel-4_19 - in the kernel source directory outside of the chroot create a symlink 'compile_commands.json' to ${CHROMIUMOS}/ chroot/build/cheza/build/kernel/compile_commands_no_chroot.json - open vscode in the kernel source directory - with the C/C++ or vscode-clangd extension vscode performs live syntax checks as a source file is modified - open kernel source directory as project in CLion - symbol search only shows results for target platform Cq-Depend: chromium:1696541 Change-Id: I2e5e1eb97386913f4b68465c00978b2a68058094 Signed-off-by: Matthias Kaehlcke <mka@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1680889 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Mike Frysinger <vapier@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org>
